data.title: Sharpening creativity
data.description: Satit Kalawantavanich is a legendary graphic designer and the founder of Sam Noh, a graphic design studio, and Phenomena, a renowned advertising and film production house. He is also the creator of Propaganda, an iconic design brand famous for its playful signature character Mr.P. In his 60s, Satit established Studio Avocado which provides creative and strategic consultancy.

data.title: 4 NHA condo projects get nod
data.description: The government on Tuesday approved four apartment projects by the National Housing Authority (NHA), offering more opportunities for low-income people to access high-quality housing at a reasonable price.

data.title: Cops nab 2 for arson attack
data.description: Police have arrested a Turkish man, 31, and his ex-girlfriend, 40, a former sales manager, over an arson attack on a company in Bang Khae district of the capital.

data.title: PP demands QR codes off list ballots
data.description: People's Party (PP) list MP Parit Wacharasindhu has called for barcodes to be removed from party-list election ballots after the Constitutional Court ruled that their use was constitutional but warned that such markings could undermine public confidence in the secrecy of voting.

data.title: Huawei nabs 'excellence' gong
data.description: Huawei Thailand has won the Thailand Cybersecurity Excellence Awards 2026 in the Most Contribution category for the fifth consecutive year.

data.title: Thai envoy rebuts Cambodian claims
data.description: Thailand has accused Cambodia of making unfounded claims at the UN despite a ceasefire in place for more than nine months, and urged Phnom Penh to end border provocations and cooperate on security.

data.title: Red-shirt leaders walk free
data.description: Three red-shirt leaders have been granted amnesty for disrupting the 2009 Asean summit in Pattaya, with two released and the third's arrest warrant revoked.

data.title: Floods affect 2.6m with 22 deaths
data.description: Flooding in 29 provinces and Bangkok has affected more than 940,000 households and 2.6 million people, with 22 deaths reported as water levels continue to rise in several areas.

data.title: Polapee denies claim of meddling at reservoir
data.description: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee denied ordering Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam in Nakhon Nayok to stop releasing water, saying he merely asked whether releases could be slowed or temporarily halted to prevent downstream flooding.

data.title: Alarm bell sounds over new city plan
data.description: The Thailand Consumers Council has warned that Bangkok faces a growing risk of flooding from northern runoff, dam discharges, accumulated rainfall and high tides, and that a proposed new city plan could make matters worse by giving flood-retention areas over to housing estates and condominiums.

data.title: Anutin under fire over flooding
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is facing public criticism over the government's response to flooding in and around Bangkok following three days of continuous rain.

data.title: Premier League confirms Man City guilty of serious financial breaches
data.description: MANCHESTER (UNITED KINGDOM) - Manchester City have been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009 and 2018, it was confirmed on Tuesday.

data.title: UN to hold fourth informal poll of secretary-general candidates
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The UN Security Council met Tuesday to gauge for a fourth time support for a packed field of contenders to lead the world organization, fresh from making their pitch to world leaders who will decide their fate.

data.title: German far-right aims to lead Saxony-Anhalt govt in December
data.description: BERLIN - The leader of the far-right AfD in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt said Tuesday he hopes to become state premier in December after the party's crushing election victory earlier this month.

data.title: Thai Airways cancels 37 more flights
data.description: Thai Airways International has cancelled 37 more domestic and international flights scheduled for Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday as it tries to dig itself out from under a massive baggage backlog at Suvarnabhumi airport.

data.title: Eiffel Tower chief to step down after ‘hiding’ female staff
data.description: PARIS - The operating company that runs the Eiffel Tower said on Tuesday that its chief would step down at the end of this year in the wake of a controversy over the removal of women staff during a visit by a Hindu religious group.

data.title: Golden Kunlavut is king of the court
data.description: Kunlavut Vitidsarn became the first Thai athlete to win the badminton men’s singles gold medal at the Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 yesterday, completing a day of triple joy for the Kingdom after earlier golds in men’s regu sepak takraw and esports.

data.title: Clashes break out as French school blockades intensify
data.description: PARIS - French teenagers on Tuesday set fire to rubbish bins and hurled projectiles at police who responded with batons and tear gas, as pupils kept up blockades and protests at hundreds of high schools, demanding better conditions.

data.title: Waterways overflow in northern Bangkok and nearby
data.description: People living near waterways in Nonthaburi and Pathum Thani provinces as well as adjacent districts of Bangkok have been warned to move belongings to higher ground as water levels are rising.

data.title: Tom Cruise trades stunts for satire as toxic tycoon ‘Digger’
data.description: PARIS - Tom Cruise is taking on one of his riskiest roles in decades, tackling the politics of climate change and corporate greed in new film “Digger”, in which he plays an embattled, ageing tycoon.

data.title: WHO says Yemen health system at ‘breaking point’
data.description: GENEVA - The escalating fighting in Yemen is pushing the country’s health system to “breaking point”, the World Health Organization said on Tuesday, warning that diseases like cholera were already circulating widely.

data.title: ‘Exceptional’ Turner painting shown in Rome
data.description: ROME - A particularly well-preserved painting of Rome by the British artist JMW Turner went on display in the city on Tuesday for the first time ahead of an auction in December.

data.title: Spain to ban evictions until 2030 amid housing protests
data.description: MADRID - Spain’s government, under pressure from nationwide housing protests, on Tuesday approved measures including a proposed ban on evictions until 2030 and the automatic renewal of tenant contracts, a minister said.
